annotations.description: Playing Island instead of Thriving Isle on turn 2 (first land drop) means that when Thriving Isle is played on turn 3, it enters tapped, leaving only 1 untapped mana on turn 3. This delays all three 3-drops (Reckless Scholar, Sailor of Means, Selhoff Occultist) by a full turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Island as first land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Isle (tapped) now, then Island untapped on turn 3 to have 2 mana available and cast a 3-drop on turn 4 on curve. Spectral Sailor can be deployed later since there's no urgent need for a 1/1 on turn 2.

annotations.description: Spectral Sailor has flash and should be cast at the end of the opponent's turn rather than in your own precombat main phase. There is no benefit to casting it now - it has summoning sickness regardless, and waiting preserves information and keeps options open (e.g., if opponent plays something worth responding to differently).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Spectral Sailor during own precombat main phase on turn 2
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn, then cast Spectral Sailor at the end of the opponent's turn to preserve information and flexibility while getting the same board result.

annotations.description: Thermo-Alchemist is generally the stronger play in a UR spells deck, especially with Goblin Wizardry (an instant) in hand. Thermo-Alchemist provides repeatable damage each turn and untaps whenever an instant or sorcery is cast, enabling multiple pings per turn. With Goblin Wizardry, Kinetic Augur, and the overall spell-heavy nature of the deck, Thermo-Alchemist's value compounds significantly over the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Heartfire Immolator (2/2 prowess with sacrifice ability)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Thermo-Alchemist, which provides repeatable damage and synergizes powerfully with the instants and sorceries in hand, particularly Goblin Wizardry which would allow double-pinging in a single turn.

annotations.description: Playing Island instead of Thriving Isle delays casting a 3-drop by a full turn. With Thriving Isle played now (enters tapped), next turn the player would have 3 mana available (2 lands untapping + new Island). With Island played now, next turn they'd play Thriving Isle (tapped) and only have 2 mana, unable to cast any of their four 3-mana spells until turn 6.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Isle (choosing red for future flexibility) this turn. It enters tapped but next turn play Island to have 3 mana available, enabling Reckless Scholar, Rishadan Airship, Sailor of Means, or Selhoff Occultist on turn 5.

annotations.description: Playing Mountain instead of Thriving Bluff on a turn where the only planned play (Thermo-Alchemist at 1R) only requires 2 mana. Thriving Bluff enters tapped but would cost zero tempo this turn since 2 Mountains are already untapped. Playing it now would bank a dual land for future blue mana needs while saving the Mountain for a turn when untapped mana matters more.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Bluff (choosing blue) — it enters tapped but you still have 2 untapped Mountains for Thermo-Alchemist, and you set up blue mana for future draws at no tempo cost.

annotations.description: Chose Green for Thriving Isle's secondary color, but their deck appears to be UR (blue-red) based on the card reference showing multiple red cards like Thermo-Alchemist, Goblin Wizardry, Kinetic Augur. Green mana has no use in their deck. Red would allow this land to help cast red spells when drawn.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Green as the secondary color for Thriving Isle
annotations.betterLine: Choose Red as the secondary color for Thriving Isle to support the red splash/component of their UR deck

annotations.description: Discarding Island when holding a hand full of 3-mana spells with only 4 lands on board. The 5th land would enable double-spelling or using Spectral Sailor's draw ability (3U) alongside deploying threats. Selhoff Occultist is the weakest card in hand - a 2/3 with mostly irrelevant mill, outclassed by Sailor of Means.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Selhoff Occultist to keep the 5th land, enabling faster hand deployment and Spectral Sailor activations alongside casting spells.

annotations.description: Timed out on Thriving Bluff's color choice. As a UR deck, Blue is the only correct choice - all other options (White, Black, Green) make the land a strictly worse Mountain that enters tapped. The timeout likely assigned a wrong color, permanently losing the dual-land utility.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) on Thriving Bluff color selection, likely receiving a non-Blue default.
annotations.betterLine: Choose Blue, the only other color in the deck, to have access to both red and blue mana from this land.

annotations.description: Libby cast Waterknot before playing their Island land drop. With a land drop available and Island in hand, the correct sequencing is always to play the land first, then cast spells. Playing Island first would give 4 total untapped mana (UUUU), cast Waterknot for 1UU, and leave U open for potential responses or end-of-turn plays. There's no benefit to casting the spell before the land drop.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Waterknot before playing the Island from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island first, then cast Waterknot with 1 mana still available.

annotations.description: Waterknot targeted Heartfire Immolator instead of Thermo-Alchemist. Thermo-Alchemist is a repeatable damage engine that doesn't need to attack, synergizes with the opponent's spells, and can't be blocked or traded in combat. Heartfire Immolator is a vanilla 2/2 in combat that can be dealt with through normal means. The Whelp's flying is also a bigger problem since most of Libby's creatures are ground-based, but Thermo-Alchemist is the most dangerous long-term.
annotations.betterLine: Put Waterknot on Thermo-Alchemist, which is a persistent unblockable damage source that will compound over many turns, especially with the opponent's instant/sorcery-heavy deck

annotations.description: Declined to sacrifice Heartfire Immolator in response to Waterknot's ETB trigger. If Waterknot targets the Immolator, it will be permanently locked down and wasted. Sacrificing it would deal 2 damage and potentially strand the Waterknot. Even if Waterknot targets another creature, sacrificing the Immolator to deal 2 damage to the opponent (at 14 life) while you have the mana available is worth considering, as the Immolator may get locked down or removed later without value.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, allowing Waterknot's ETB to resolve without sacrificing Heartfire Immolator.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Heartfire Immolator's sacrifice ability targeting the opponent (or a relevant creature) to get 2 damage value, especially if Waterknot is enchanting the Immolator itself.

annotations.description: Cast Goblin Wizardry before activating Thermo-Alchemist. By tapping Thermo-Alchemist first (1 damage), then casting Goblin Wizardry (which untaps Thermo-Alchemist as an instant/sorcery), then tapping again (1 damage), DSV3 would deal 2 damage from Thermo-Alchemist instead of potentially only 1. Casting the spell first wastes the untap trigger if Thermo-Alchemist is already untapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Goblin Wizardry before activating Thermo-Alchemist
annotations.betterLine: Activate Thermo-Alchemist first (1 damage to opponent), then cast Goblin Wizardry (untaps Thermo-Alchemist), then activate Thermo-Alchemist again (1 more damage), then go to combat and attack with Sarkhan's Whelp

annotations.description: Thermo-Alchemist is currently untapped and its untap trigger from casting Goblin Wizardry is on the stack. By tapping Thermo-Alchemist now to deal 1 damage before the untap trigger resolves, Valley would get a free extra ping (the untap trigger would then untap it again for future use). By passing, the untap trigger resolves on an already-untapped creature and does nothing, wasting 1 free damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, letting the untap trigger resolve while Thermo-Alchemist was already untapped.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Thermo-Alchemist to deal 1 damage to the opponent, then let the untap trigger resolve to untap it again, netting 1 free damage.

annotations.description: Declined to activate Thermo-Alchemist to deal 1 free damage to the opponent (14 life). Thermo-Alchemist's tap ability costs no mana and deals 1 damage to each opponent. With Goblin Wizardry on the stack (an instant), the Thermo-Alchemist untap trigger likely already resolved or will resolve, meaning activating now would be pure upside - deal 1 damage now, and it untaps when the spell resolves or when another instant/sorcery is cast later.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Thermo-Alchemist, missing 1 free damage.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Thermo-Alchemist to deal 1 damage to the opponent before passing priority, since it's a free activation that costs no mana.

annotations.description: With Goblin Wizardry (an instant/sorcery) on the stack, Thermo-Alchemist could have been tapped now to deal 1 damage, then it would untap when Goblin Wizardry resolves (triggering its 'whenever you cast an instant or sorcery, untap' ability), allowing a second activation later. By passing, DSV3 Valley missed 1 extra point of damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Thermo-Alchemist while Goblin Wizardry was on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Thermo-Alchemist to deal 1 damage to opponent before Goblin Wizardry resolves, getting an extra ping since Thermo-Alchemist would untap on resolution of the instant spell.

annotations.description: Cast Selhoff Occultist (2/3 with irrelevant mill ability) instead of Sailor of Means (1/4 + Treasure token) when at 11 life facing an aggressive board with multiple attackers. The 1/4 body blocks ground threats much more effectively, and the Treasure token provides crucial mana flexibility for future turns (enabling double-spell turns or holding up interaction).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Selhoff Occultist (2/3 with mill trigger)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sailor of Means to get a 1/4 blocker and a Treasure token, better stabilizing at 11 life against the opponent's aggressive board

annotations.description: Failed to activate Thermo-Alchemist to deal 1 damage to the opponent before the stack resolves. The opponent is at 10 life, and this free point of damage (bringing them to 7 instead of 8 after Hungry Flames) has no downside since Thermo-Alchemist has defender, can't attack, and there's no way to untap it again this turn (only Kinetic Augur, a creature, is in hand).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Thermo-Alchemist, missing 1 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Thermo-Alchemist to deal 1 damage to opponent before letting the stack resolve, dealing a total of 3 damage to the opponent this turn instead of 2.

annotations.description: DSV3 Valley declined to activate Thermo-Alchemist to deal 1 damage to the opponent for free. With Hungry Flames already cast (triggering the untap), Thermo-Alchemist was available to tap for 1 damage. With only Kinetic Augur (a creature) in hand and no more instants/sorceries to cast, there was no reason to hold the activation. This wastes 1 point of free damage against an opponent at 10 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Thermo-Alchemist, leaving 1 free damage on the table.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Thermo-Alchemist to deal 1 damage to the opponent before Hungry Flames resolves, bringing the total damage this turn to 9 (opponent goes to 1) instead of 8 (opponent goes to 2).

annotations.description: At 1 life, Grok4F Libby timed out and took no action. The opponent's Thermo-Alchemist will untap next turn and tap to deal 1 damage, killing Libby. Sweep Away was available to bounce the Thermo-Alchemist, which was the only way to survive. Additionally, creatures like Sailor of Means or Reckless Scholar could have been deployed as blockers against the opponent's attackers.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed without casting any spells.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sweep Away targeting Thermo-Alchemist to prevent guaranteed lethal next turn, then cast Reckless Scholar with remaining 2 mana as an additional blocker.
